subject: Acme: embeddings p95/p99 latency surge following catalog patch - urgent
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: sudden jump in embeddings p99 after morning catalog update

Monica,

We started seeing a large increase in p95/p99 latency on the embeddings endpoint this morning around 07:30 PT. Some jobs that normally finish <200ms are taking 800ms-1.4s. Error rates are unchanged but throughput is degraded for our bulk vectorize pipeline. This started right after you confirmed the new model-catalog patch rolled at ~07:15.

Can you confirm whether Redwood pushed any catalog variants or routing changes today? We're blocked on an overnight batch and this is impacting an internal release.

- Alex
Alex Turner
Platform Lead, Acme Corp
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden jump in embeddings p99 after morning catalog update

Thanks for flagging, Alex — really sorry you're hitting this. I'm escalating internally and looping in platform and support to investigate.

Initial ask: Ben/Markus/Laura, can you confirm (1) whether a catalog commit/patch rolled to prod at ~07:15 PT for models that serve embeddings endpoints for Acme, (2) if any routing/fallback policy was changed, and (3) whether we can provide a quick rollback if needed.

Alex, attaching a short sampling request: could you send one or two representative request IDs or a small batch of the vectors that timed out? That will help us reproduce.

Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden jump in embeddings p99 after morning catalog update

Monica — short version: yes, we pushed a model-catalog patch at 07:12 that included two quantized variants and a routing tweak that promoted the smaller-quantized variant for cost reasons on certain routes.

Observed symptoms so far: p95 and p99 for embeddings spiked at ~07:30, correlating with an uptick in requests routed to the newly promoted variant. No error-rate increase, but CPU/GPU utilization on the promoted pool increased unevenly leading to queuing.

Immediate actions in flight:
- Rolling back routing promotion for Acme's routing key (will take a few minutes to drain)
- Capturing KV-cache metrics and per-shard queue depth
- Exporting sample traces to acme_embedding_sample_logs.txt (attached)

I will update in 15. If rollback looks safe we can fallback to the previous catalog state for Acme only.

— Ben
Ben Carter
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden jump in embeddings p99 after morning catalog update

Thanks for the quick response, Ben. I just uploaded three example request IDs and a small CSV of client-side timestamps to ops+data@acme.com; please let me know if you need raw payloads.

Our SLAs are tight on latency for this customer-facing pipeline. If rollback helps, we'd prefer that — we can tolerate a brief drain window.

- Alex
From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden jump in embeddings p99 after morning catalog update

Update: Started rollback for Acme routing at 09:16; changes are propagating. Early telemetry shows p95 dropping from ~680ms to ~220ms within a single minute on several shards. We're continuing a careful staged rollback to avoid cache churn.

Note: the promoted quantized variant had a regression on long-sequence attention warmup in our environment — KV-cache priming for vectorize workloads is heavier and caused queuing on a subset of trace lengths. We're preparing a targeted patch to the quantization priming logic.

I've uploaded a concise rollback plan (prod-rollback-plan.md) and a quick SLO impact CSV (slo-impact-summary.csv) to the incident Drive link.

-Markus
Platform Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden jump in embeddings p99 after morning catalog update

Thanks team — rolling status to Acme: we've initiated rollback and are seeing recovery signals. Monica, can you confirm whether we should offer a goodwill credit or an SLA exception? Vanessa, can you prep a short note for Alex summarizing timeline and next steps (inc. fix ETA and rollback window details) 

Alex: we will follow up with a formal incident summary and proposed credits after we validate full recovery. Apologies for the disruption.

- Laura
Customer Support, Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden jump in embeddings p99 after morning catalog update

Alex — quick closure note: rollback completed at 12:04 PT; our monitoring shows p95/p99 back within expected ranges and batch throughput normalized. Attached are the sample logs and the rollback plan.

Next steps: (1) Markus will ship a targeted priming patch for the quantized variant (ETA 48 hours) (2) we'll schedule a controlled canary that exercises Acme's vectorize distribution before any promotion (3) Customer Success will propose a one-time credit for the impacted window.

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute postmortem with engineering to walk the telemetry. Again, really sorry for the disruption — appreciate the partnership and quick reporting.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
